summary: A Safe's batch calls execTransaction on a child Safe that it created, solely owns, and funded, which transfers the child's tokens; only the parent-child interaction is considered, since a transaction of the child needs its own Safenet proposal, and the child is in the parent's expected target set; secure under R-4.3.
---

Safe 0x5317B52D3bFEA2d9C26F756C431A78929088B32f (the Parent Safe) on Ethereum Mainnet (chain ID 1), Safe transaction 0x70992c78cd0681c643e0f9db997122f2b42ce1ce0aae2e5de959bfe3f1905117 (nonce 126), under Charter bafkreigg6ajqdb52kb644wcxegurt7r6jlclru4mjy3lwxkbh6avm3vgre. The disputed rule is R-4.3, which the only insecure vote cites. The transaction delegate calls MultiSendCallOnly 1.3.0, which makes six value-0 calls of execTransaction on the Safe 0xb09bfa2e0731996866aae22733cb8c8185d72a7c (the Child Safe), each transferring the Child Safe's tokens of 0xe6bfd33f52d82ccb5b37e16d3dd81f9ffdabb195 to 0x63e3d1d9f8ba75fcaaae27555fb58dd981dd89ab. The transaction moves none of the Parent Safe's own value and pays no refund. The Council holds that when a Safe transaction executes a transaction of another Safe, it considers only the proposing Safe's interaction with that Child Safe, and never the Child Safe's own transaction (§ 2.3). If the Child Safe were Safenet-enabled, its transaction would need its own Safenet proposal, with the Child Safe as the proposing Safe. A transaction through a Parent Safe and a Child Safe that are both Safenet-enabled therefore needs two attestations. The Council considers the Child Safe as the target of this transaction (§ 2.4). The Child Safe is not merely an intermediate contract but a Safe that holds the tokens and executes its own transactions, and it is in the Parent Safe's expected target set (§ 2.4, § 2.9):
- the Parent Safe created it (ProxyCreation event in transaction 0x635046bc35639b68a058e92a83f70814eceb3f8abcc970edc926e4941330eeec, block 24322119);
- the Parent Safe is its sole owner, with a threshold of 1;
- the Parent Safe funded it with the same token at nonces 85 and 86;
- 48 of the 49 other Safes that the Parent Safe's earlier executions call with execTransaction are Safes that it created and funded.
Applying 0x298149bb3e95eb950dfb281185f338dcf91f1d3585ad9c6ec22ace33b668c7e3 (secure) by analogy, where the Safe's own owner was in the expected target set, here a Safe that the Safe owns is in it. Distinguishing 0x844fe527e82fbf88b70e05db4c487de8143ca5d3b97e2eca24f6348c4d894434 (insecure), whose Safe had no history and no link to its payee. The Council finds no evidence-grounded failure of R-4.3 (§ 3.7) and rules the transaction secure. This is a novel fact pattern. The Council records it as precedent and flags it for possible amendment by SafeDAO (§ 5.1).
